claims.text: The person the walkthrough was written for asked how the owner makes his AI sound so human.
claims.quote: how do you make your AI sound so human?

claims.text: The voice is not a setting; it is a corpus, a memo, a short list of rules and a reader who corrects, and it stops working if any one is removed.
claims.quote: It is a corpus, a memo, a short list of rules, and a reader who corrects.

claims.text: The corpus is 86 articles on the site, about 347,000 words, each citing the ones before it.
claims.quote: 86 articles on this site, about 347,000 words, 51 of them starting as a voice memo

claims.text: 51 of the 86 articles began as a voice memo and say so.
claims.quote: 51 of them starting as a voice memo and saying so

claims.text: The memo is the biggest of the four inputs and where most of the voice comes from.
claims.quote: This is my hypothesis, and I think it is the biggest of the four.

claims.text: A typed brief is already edited into someone else's register; a memo is how the owner thinks, in the order he thinks it, with the phrases he would use.
claims.quote: A typed brief is already edited into someone else's register.

claims.text: There are seven wording rules, each a correction made once, now a line in the session's behaviour policy restored after every summary.
claims.quote: Seven of them, and each one was a correction I made once.

claims.text: The site's validator checks some of the rules at build time, so a banned word cannot reach the page.
claims.quote: the site's validator checks some of them at build time, so a word I have banned cannot reach the page

claims.text: The owner reads every article, usually twice, before it goes live and once on the site; a jarring word becomes a rule and a wrong point a new version.
claims.quote: I read every article, usually twice: once before it goes live and once on the site.

claims.text: The model never decides whether something sounds like the owner; the owner does.
claims.quote: The model never decides whether something sounds like me. I do.

claims.text: Since the session's last summary the owner sent 98 messages, 25 of them over 300 words, five of them Otter transcripts of about 4,900 words.
claims.quote: there have been 98 messages from me, 25 of them over 300 words

claims.text: Of the corrections in the last two days, one was about a word; the rest were about content and direction.
claims.quote: one in the last two days was about a word: "prose".

claims.text: In the earlier weeks the balance was the other way: em-dashes, perfect, the ladder word and massively were each caught and turned into a rule.
claims.quote: In the earlier weeks the balance was the other way.

claims.text: A language correction is made once and then enforced; a content correction is about this article and has to be made again, because it is new thinking.
claims.quote: a language correction is made once and then enforced; a content correction is about this article and has to be made again next time

claims.text: What the model does when it writes as the owner is not imitation; the difference from writing like X is the context.
claims.quote: What I am doing is not imitation.

claims.text: A model given only a style sample produces surface resemblance, which is why it usually sounds like a parody.
claims.quote: That is a thin thing, and it is why it usually sounds like a parody.

claims.text: A typed brief tells the model what to write; a memo tells it how the owner got there, so the tangent is the connection he made, not noise.
claims.quote: A typed brief tells me what to write. A memo tells me how he got there.

claims.text: The corrections are specific, and the policy file means the model does not have to remember them across a summary; the harness prints them back.
claims.quote: the policy file means I do not have to remember them across a summary, which I cannot reliably do; the harness prints them back

claims.text: Nothing has been trained; the model is the one anyone else uses and what differs is one session's context.
claims.quote: Nothing has been trained. I am the same model anyone else uses.

claims.text: The voice cannot be given to another author without their articles, their memos, their banned words and their reading, which takes weeks that are mostly theirs.
claims.quote: That takes weeks, and most of the weeks are theirs, not mine.

claims.text: The counts are one session's, after its last summary; earlier sessions are summarised, not counted.
claims.quote: The counts are one session's, after its last summary.

claims.text: The model's account of itself is an account, not a measurement; it cannot see why the context works inside the model.
claims.quote: The model's account of itself is an account, not a measurement.

claims.text: Whether the articles sound like the owner is judged by the owner alone; nobody else has been asked.
claims.quote: "Sounds like me" is judged by me.

claims.text: Nothing is trained: the voice is context and ends with the session, which is why the rules live in a file and the articles on a site.
claims.quote: The voice is context, and it ends with the session

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 12 October 2026 after showing the walkthrough to the person it was written for, who is not named.
claims.quote: after showing the walkthrough to the person it was written for; she is not named
